toast.$comment: A toast is a piece of the page that has arrived on top of it — the popover's surface rather than the tooltip's inverted one, and for the popover's reason: the message is something the user reads and may act on, not an annotation on a control they are pointing at. What is different from every other panel here is that nothing anchors it, so the two numbers no other component needs are the distance from the window's edge and the layer it sits on.
toast.$comment-inset: How far the stack stands off the window's edge. One token for both axes: a toast in the corner is inset from two edges at once, and a skin that wants it tighter wants it tighter in both.

inset.$description: Distance of the toast from the edge of the viewport.

toast.$comment-gap: Between two toasts. It is what says they are separate messages rather than one panel with several lines — the shadow alone does not, since a shadow falls on the toast below it.
toast.$comment-z-index: Above the CDK overlay container — the dependency's own number, read from its stylesheet by `check-tokens` on every run and held below this one (`layers.policy.json`): a message raised by a dialog's own save button has to be visible over that dialog, and a toast behind a modal is a message nobody reads. It is a token and not a number in the sheet because an application with a layer of its own above ours has nowhere else to say so.
toast.$comment-item-border: The popover's argument exactly: the toast stands on the page rather than over a veil, so this line is the only thing separating a light panel from a light page, and a shadow is not that thing — it goes with the mode that takes shadows away.
toast.$comment-item-max-width: Wider than a tooltip and narrower than a popover: a toast is a sentence about something that has just happened, and a panel as wide as a dialog would cover the corner of the page the user is still working in.

item-gap.$description: Gap between a toast's message and its action.

toast.$comment-icon: The tone's drawing and the colour it takes. The ICON is the tone — a message painted in colour alone is a state carried by colour alone (`req-a11y-forced-colors`), and a reader who cannot tell red from green, or a forced palette that throws both away, still has the shape (plan 4.14). The base `icon-fg` is the message's own text colour, which is what a toast with no tone would draw if it ever drew one: the four variants below are the only reason this token exists.
toast.$comment-icon-size: One `em` would tie the drawing to the message's font size, which is `sm`; a message that is a sentence and an icon that is a road sign do not scale together. A dimension of its own, and the same 16px the close cross is drawn on.
toast.$comment-item-border-tones: The edge takes the tone too, and that is not a second channel — it is the same one, louder. What makes the tone legible is the drawing beside the sentence; the border is what makes it visible from across a room, and it is measured against the page like the untoned edge above it.
toast.$comment-action-fg: The one thing on a toast that can be pressed for a reason other than making it go away, so it is the page's accent — and it is measured against the toast's own surface rather than against the page's, which is the same colour today and need not stay so.

action-fg.$description: Text colour of the action button.

action-font-weight.$description: Font weight of the action button.

action-radius.$description: Corner radius of the action button.

close-fg.$description: Text colour of the close button.

close-fg-hover.$description: Text colour of the close button on hover.

close-bg-hover.$description: Background of the close button on hover.

close-radius.$description: Corner radius of the close button.

toast.$comment-close-size: The box, not the cross: the drawing is 16px and the target the pointer has to hit is `pct.target.min` (req-a11y-touch).
